Subject: Re: Production 5xx/429 spike + timeouts - need immediate help

Short triage update — attaching a small excerpt of our edge logs.

What we see:
- A large burst of downstream TCP timeouts and connection resets to Acme's VPC IPs starting ~09:28 PDT.
- HAProxy error rate (5xx) tracks with increased upstream tcp retransmits.
- 429s are coming from our internal rate-limiter kicking in after retries pile up.

Hypothesis: symptoms are consistent with NAT/gateway exhaustion or intermittent blackholing on the peering path (NAT conntrack table filling -> new connections dropped -> client retries -> rate limiting).

Immediate mitigations we can run now:
1) Apply a temporary token-bucket limiter at the LB to slow retries (drops non-essential retries).
2) Enable short-circuit fallback that routes a percentage of traffic to hosted endpoints to relieve the dedicated pool (need Marissa approval).
3) Request Acme SRE to share VPC Flow Logs for the 09:00–10:00 window and check NAT gateway CloudWatch metrics / conntrack.

Attachments: acme_edge_errors_excerpt.log

-Sean
Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge@acmehealth.com>, acme-sre@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-03-09T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production 5xx/429 spike + timeouts - need immediate help

Quick infra analysis from the dedicated cluster and edge:
- Observed repeated DNS resolution failures to regional-dedicated-acme.redwood-infra.net (timeouts + SERVFAIL) coincident with the error spike.
- NAT gateway metrics show conntrack table approaching capacity (approx 96% used) for the subnet serving this deployment.
- Health checks for a subset of the dedicated instances started flapping; backend connection attempts returned ECONNRESET.
- There are signs of a retry storm: client retries + our internal LB retries created amplified load.

Likely root cause: intermittent connectivity / NAT connection tracking exhaustion combined with peering route flaps. DNS timeouts may be a separate symptom (resolver path intermittent) or a cascading effect when backends drop connections.

Immediate steps I recommend (with timeline):
A) Apply token-bucket limiter at LB (5–10 min). Will reduce retry amplification.
B) Provision an extra NAT gateway / scale conntrack (30–45 min) — requires coordination with Acme or permission to add egress NAT on their side if they control it.
C) Failover 25–50% of traffic to hosted endpoints (10–20 min) — lowest disruption and fastest relief.
D) Continue collection of VPC Flow Logs & traceroutes — Acme SRE please share logs.

I'm prepared to implement A and C now if we get sign-off from Marissa / Acme.

-David
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-03-10T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Exec notice & immediate mitigation plan for Acme outage

Evelyn — I need a quick sign-off to execute mitigations and to notify our executives / legal for potential SLA credits. Acme is seeing elevated 5xx/429 caused by what looks like a dedicated/private networking issue (VPC peering + NAT conntrack).

Planned immediate actions (requesting approval):
- Apply token-bucket rate-limiting at the LB (reduce retry amplification) — operational impact minimal.
- Failover 40% of Acme traffic to hosted endpoints for 2 hours to stabilize customer traffic and buy time for joint debugging.
- Ask Acme to scale NAT / check firewall conntrack and share VPC Flow Logs; we'll provide explicit runbook steps.
- Send executive notification to Acme (Jorge) and Redwood execs summarizing actions, impact, and crediting plan if SLA threshold crossed.

Rationale: failover buys us 1–2 hours of buffer without doing risky infra changes in the customer's VPC. We should prepare a credit calculation (pro-rated) if total downtime breaches SLO.

Evelyn, please reply 'approve' or 'no' — if no reply in 15 min, we'll proceed with A (LB limiter) and C (partial failover) to stabilize.

—Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge@acmehealth.com>, acme-sre@acmehealth.com

Date: 2026-03-10T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Actioned: partial failover + rate-limit applied — monitoring impact

Jorge — quick update and apologize again for the disruption. Actions taken at 09:30 PDT:
- Applied token-bucket rate limiter at edge LB to reduce retry amplification.
- Failed over 40% of Acme traffic to our hosted endpoints (we kept 60% on dedicated to preserve locality).
- Ongoing: collecting VPC Flow Logs and DNS traces (INFRA-5789).

Early results: 5xx/429 rates down ~78% at edge (see attached haproxy-metrics-2026-03-09.png). We continue to monitor for any regressions.

Next steps:
- Redwood infra will work with Acme SRE to increase NAT conntrack capacity and review peering/firewall rules.
- We'll schedule a joint RFC to update route and NAT sizing and provide a permanent remediation plan (target: complete by 2026-03-17).
- I'll send the executive summary and a proposed credit calculation if SLA thresholds were exceeded.
